issue10.title: STAGE 03 / SURFACE.00 — Surface Material Painting architecture (research only)
issue10.body:
# Stage 03 / SURFACE.00 — ARCHITECTURE RESEARCH ONLY; NO ADDON IMPLEMENTATION AUTHORIZED

> **OWNER PRODUCT PIVOT — 23 October 2026 (supersedes the 15 October priority).** GO_FLORA is now an Unreal-inspired **environment authoring tool**, with existing Foliage/Object Paint plus **Surface Material Painting** as its next major direction, and optional later Mesh Paint and foliage-by-surface-layer rules. Full tree/shrub/texture/material generation and Tree3D provider development are **removed from the active GO_FLORA roadmap**. GAME_FLORA remains a separate Blender addon. Unreal Foliage/Landscape Paint/Mesh Paint are workflow references, **not full MVP parity commitments**. The owner authorized **design/research work only**; no modifications to `addons/go_flora`, TEST_FLORA, PR #19, merge/release or Stage 04 implementation.

**Current engineering gate, 23 Oct:** main 0.2.5-dev at `d911087157ecaa9e3ab2b92d95049f2999aebab1`; Source Identity Issue #18 / PR #19 OPEN, head `7093b07922999778d01b3afa49ebc4272cc10cde`, candidate 0.2.6-dev, owner interactive QA **NOT_RUN**. Stage 02 was accepted with Issue #12 deferred QA; Issue #15 remains a separate UX backlog. Design research may proceed without treating PR #19 as merged. The new roadmap is maintained in [document 11](https://docs.google.com/document/d/12j2p5CuVLecJ66iFDDJ99gPcaD1AF2IAU-d0t4r_zUs/edit), with the revised product contract in [document 18](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fkWorFG1pNALeVlCUWD2sTk9DmHgrMl7ZeCuVeohDaA/edit).

## Historical design context (15 October 2026; updated scope above has precedence)

**Product decision (owner, 15 October 2026):** Add the future capability to paint and blend ground **surface materials in layers**, conceptually analogous to **Unreal Engine Landscape Layer Painting**. The design must be **terrain-independent**, consistent with ADR 0001, and co-exist with the current Foliage Painter. The original proposal was to reserve this before adding tree generation and Texture Lab; **the 23 October owner decision supersedes those expansion plans.**

**Design document v0.1 (Google Drive, project knowledge base):** [18 — GO_FLORA | Surface Material Painting](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fkWorFG1pNALeVlCUWD2sTk9DmHgrMl7ZeCuVeohDaA/edit)  
**Project:** https://github.com/alekseypilishkov-gif/go_flora  
**Existing ADR 0001:** [Editor-first logical data with optional plant providers](https://github.com/alekseypilishkov-gif/go_flora/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE_ADR_0001.md)  
**Historical Stage 02 reference:** PR #6 is MERGED; Stage 02 now FINALIZED / ACCEPTED_WITH_DEFERRED_QA. PR #14 and PR #17 MERGED. Issue #18 / PR #19 awaits owner GUI QA. **Tree3D is no longer the planned Stage 03; revised Stage 03 is this Surface Architecture Research.**

## User-facing goal

Select a ground material layer (Grass / Dirt / Rock / Mud; potentially Snow overlay) in a dedicated **Surface** paint mode, then hold LMB and brush a blended material directly onto an existing collision-backed mesh ground, as in Unreal Landscape Paint Mode. Surface painting does **not** place 3D grass; the separate Foliage mode does that.

## Proposed design seams (DRAFT; not final class/API contract)

- Two exclusive Painter modes: **Foliage** (already shipping) and **Surface** (future). The latter gets its own material palette, SurfacePaintTarget, per-surface authoritative mask data, shaders and undoable strokes; **do not modify GFInstanceRecord schema 1 or GFVegetationSet**.
- Terrain-independent but NOT universally arbitrary geometry: initial support for ground-like `MeshInstance3D` + matching collider, simple target material slot and stable local planar XZ mapping. Vertical walls/caves, UV islands, overlapping floors, GridMap, CSG, multiple materials and Terrain3D adapters require separate capability analysis and explicit diagnostics.
- Weight-blended material layers: up to **four proposed first-pass materials including base**, initially backed by one RGBA8 tile mask per ground patch (weights normalized to 1, deterministic fallback base). Independent overlay/alpha layers (snow/puddles) need separate channel space; data model must not preclude them.
- Stable layer IDs, material set resource reusable across surfaces, mask tile resources local to scene/target. No writing to original source Mesh, source textures or shared Material resources; managed shader material variants only, with an opt-in and reversible ownership policy.
- Two distinct texture coordinate roles: source texture UV/tile scale versus paint-mask target mapping, with different resolution and filter settings. Retro PS1/PS2 albedo preparation, if needed, is handled outside the Surface Painter from ready-made textures. Texture Lab is deferred and is not a required dependency; do not force low resolution paint masks.
- Preserve scene save/reopen and editor runtime. **External mask persistence is a hard technical gate:** Godot `ImageTexture.update` merely refreshes a texture and does not mean Ctrl+S serializes an edited external PNG. Decide a deterministic source of truth (`.res`, PNG+descriptor, etc), atomic saving, dirty state/error visibility, and Tile-Rect Undo/Redo before implementing.
- Share only low-level editor hit query/brush orchestration with existing Foliage; `GFSurfaceTarget` currently depends on `GFBrush` + `VegetationLayer3D` and must not simply be used unchanged. Material paint and foliage paint cannot handle the same LMB gesture simultaneously; editor camera/navigation remains usable.
- Future optional rule: material weights may drive density/masking of painted foliage via **read-only mask queries** and explicit user-triggered deterministic Scatter/Reconcile; painting Dirt must not delete existing grass instances silently.
- UI: keep compact, mutually exclusive Foliage / Surface tool modes. A future Material Library is selection/organization of existing material texture sets; a separate Studio is OPTIONAL, not a gate. Atlas Builder, Texture Lab and Tree Generator are outside the active scope. Do not expand the slim Painter dock into a multi-page texture editor.

## Required subsequent architecture discovery (not implementation)

1. Compare source-aligned, object-local and UV-space paint mapping. Decide precise v1 capability contract, mesh/collider and transform invariants.
2. Implementable schema prototypes: persistent surface masks, layer IDs, explicit channel mappings, versioning, safe recovery on missing/reimported resources. Consider error/undo atomicity for external image files.
3. Evaluate shader architecture on **Godot 4.7.2 Forward+, Mobile and Compatibility**, using 4 material layers and optional overlay shader separate. Don't assume prior foliage alpha-scissor GPU checks validate this.
4. Agree on material ownership, restoration, reused MaterialSet vs independent maps, risk of overlapping/duplicated ground meshes, and record/runtime packaging.
5. Specify Surface Painter UI integration and safeguards against input callbacks, modal windows and existing GO_FLORA dock regressions.
6. Stage identifier approved by owner: **Stage 03 = Surface Material Painting Architecture & Feasibility (RESEARCH ONLY)**. The old Tree3D Stage 03 has been explicitly superseded. Propose, but DO NOT implement, Stage 04 Surface Painter MVP.

## Exit of this issue at architecture stage

A reviewed ADR/design with explicit target mesh support matrix, data schema draft, mask storage/save/reopen strategy, shader proof requirements, UI ownership, regressions and a scope-limited Codex implementation proposal. **Only Stage 03 design/audit/feasibility is authorized as of 23 Oct. No add-on code changes, ZIP, merge, release, asset migration or Stage 04 implementation are authorized.** If temporary technical probes are needed, run them isolated in `.scratch`, never modifying `C:\Dev\TEST_FLORA`. Readback must distinguish confirmed evidence from design hypotheses.

Official references: [Unreal Landscape Paint](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/landscape-paint-mode-in-unreal-engine); [Unreal Landscape Materials](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/landscape-materials-in-unreal-engine); [Godot Image](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_image.html); [Godot ImageTexture](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_imagetexture.html); [Godot shader language](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/shaders/shader_reference/shading_language.html).

issue18.title: P2 — Source Identity: persist canonical .tres references instead of transient embedded copies
issue18.body:
**STATUS 2026-10-20: STAGE A ARCHITECTURE REVIEW APPROVED; STAGE B MINIMAL VARIANT A IMPLEMENTATION AUTHORIZED BY OWNER.** This header supersedes the research-only prohibition below for scoped Stage B code work. See [Stage B owner authorization](https://github.com/alekseypilishkov-gif/go_flora/issues/18#issuecomment-6289589679). Implementation may create a new branch/PR, but may NOT merge, release, run Stage03, rewrite/migrate legacy embedded resources, or change TEST_FLORA. The Stage A history and boundaries below remain preserved.

---

## GO_FLORA — Source Identity P2 / external `.tres` vs embedded scene copies

**Priority:** P2, before Stage 03 Tree Generator
**Stage:** 02 maintenance, contract-first
**Authorization:** owner asked to prepare the technical contract. **Current permission is RESEARCH + CONTRACT ONLY**; no addon edits, migration, code PR, or TEST_FLORA modification until architecture review is accepted.

### Confirmed observed defect

Read-only TEST_FLORA audit of 20.10.2026 found that after creating a Source:
- `addons/go_flora/editor/source_creator.gd::_save_source()` calls `ResourceSaver.save(source, path)`, then emits `source_saved(source)` with the **original unsaved in-memory object**.
- `addons/go_flora/editor/plugin.gd::_add_created_source()` adds this same transient object to the palette instead of binding the saved `.tres`.
- The saved standalone `.tres` and a later embedded Source inside `demo.tscn` can share the same `source_id` but differ in `allow_scene_fallback`, `reviewed_scene_revision`, materials or other fields. Audit reproduced that original Source may keep an empty `resource_path`, while `ResourceLoader.load(path)` yields a different object.
- Example: `res://authored_plant_source.tres` has `REVIEW_REQUIRED`, while `res://go_flora_stage01_demo/demo.tscn::Resource_4rbh7` with the **same** `source_id` is `REVIEWED_READY`; analog for revision QA.
- No dangerous duplicate `source_id` within a single active set was found, nor orphaned placement records.

**This is a storage / edit identity issue, not evidence of immediate data corruption or a Source fingerprint bug.** Repeating IDs across snapshots/scenes may be intentional and is not by itself an error. See user-supplied `TEST_FLORA Project Audit` (20.10.2026, F1).

### Proposed target contract (to validate and refine)

1. For **new** Source Creator creations, the `.tres` at the selected project-local path is the **canonical authored persisted Source**. After successful save, palette entry must reference that persisted resource, not the transient draft; scene save/reopen must serialize an external reference (where Godot permits) rather than silently embedding a second independently editable copy.
2. Canonical identity is **path/UID + serialized content**, not guaranteed `get_instance_id()` equality across processes or across `resource_local_to_scene` instantiation. Investigate Godot 4.7.2 `ResourceSaver.save`, `ResourceLoader.load` cache modes, UID handling, nested local-to-scene behavior before prescribing exact implementation.
3. The Source `source_id` remains stable; no renumbering, deduplication by `display_name`, or automatic reconnection of legacy embedded copies just because they happen to have the same ID.
4. Existing schema 1 scenes and inlined Source copies remain loadable, renderable and editable; **no automatic legacy migration**. Existing reviewed Scene Fallback approvals are not silently granted/revoked by loading a different copy with the same ID. Invalid/future schema stays fail-closed.
5. Creator handles Save Cancel, overwrite/filename collision, ResourceSaver errors, wrong-type reload, editor's resource cache, reimport and Undo/Redo deterministically. Failure cannot append an unpersisted Source while claiming Save succeeded. Original imported GLB/PackedScene/PNG/WebP assets are only referenced, never edited.
6. Palette/Inspector and external Source edit should have coherent outcomes after save/reopen; `render_only_sources`, other sets/scenes using the same `.tres`, reimport/revision invalidation and logical records must be evaluated. Do not assume every shared Source should update every historical embedded snapshot.
7. No changes to `GFInstanceRecord`, placement IDs/transforms, set IDs, Source Kind enum values, Scene Fallback allowlist/approval, fingerprint/revision algorithm, renderer eligibility, public schema or brush/Erase semantics.
8. Physical owner QA uses **one** `C:\Dev\TEST_FLORA` project and **one** main scene `res://go_flora_stage01_demo/demo.tscn`, with reversible changes and no separate owner test project. Codex automated fixtures may run in disposable isolated directories but never modify owner TEST_FLORA.

### Mandatory Stage A — READ-ONLY architecture investigation

- Verify reproducer against **current main `d911087157ecaa9e3ab2b92d95049f2999aebab1`** (GO_FLORA 0.2.5-dev). Read `AGENTS.md`, `docs/STAGE_02_SOURCE_CONTRACTS.md`, creator/palette/scene serialization, and existing Stage 01/02 tests.
- On disposable test fixture, test exact source identity/serialization for Mesh, PackedScene REVIEW_REQUIRED + REVIEWED_READY, AlphaCard PNG/WebP, same `.tres` across sets/scenes; ResourceSaver+ResourceLoader cache; subresource references; `resource_local_to_scene`; repeated Inspector edits/save/reopen/reimport; Save Cancel/errors/overwrite.
- Document actual Godot behavior as **CONFIRMED** only with commands and evidence. Label assumptions/interpretations INFERRED and UNKNOWN. Include before/after `.tscn` textual `ExtResource` vs `SubResource` evidence and Source IDs/revisions.
- Produce design options (minimum scoped patch vs more intrusive refactor) with tradeoffs, risks, explicit ownership & migration policy, automated test matrix, and owner GUI acceptance in one scene.
- **STOP for owner architecture approval**. Do not change addon, run migration, create code PR, merge, release or start Stage 03 merely because this Issue exists. Keep user's local worktree and untracked files intact; no forced checkout/pull/reset. If latest main is inaccessible without modifying local working state, report blocker.

### Later Stage B — only after separate owner approval

Implement scoped fix on branch based on current main, tests/regressions/CI, plugin-only dev ZIP + SHA256, PR, then owner interactive QA. No auto merge.

**Related issues:** #15 placement-only removal (separate), #12 deferred QA (separate). Previous #14 and #17 are merged in main.
